- Unit pricing: per-site vs per-node vs per-GPU SKU breakdown (including minimums)
- Platform fee schedule and an amortization example (how you suggest customers account for the platform fee over 12/24/36 months)
- Support tiers: what's included in Standard vs Premium vs Enterprise (on‑call hours, patch windows, response SLAs)
- Any one-time engineering support/implementation credits you can offer for pilots or multi-site rollouts

Also, we have an internal requirement to see an example SOW and any standard escrow/escrow-adjacent language you use for on‑prem binaries. Last thing — will you be able to provide SOC2 evidence and the KMS/SSO integration notes for our security team?

Target timeline: procurement is aiming to finalize commercial terms by 2027-05-31. Curious what flexibility you have on pilot credits and platform fee amortization.

Hi Anna — really appreciate the clear checklist. Attaching a concise pricing workbook that breaks down the options and an SOW draft for a starter pilot so your legal team has something to review. Quick summary here to make procurement modeling easier: 

1) Pricing constructs (summary)
- Site license: fixed fee per physical site (recommended for multi-tenant datacenters where GPU counts vary). Includes unlimited nodes within site boundary; good for predictable CapEx.
- Node license: per-node (licensed per machine) — ideal for lift-and-shift modern infra. Scales linearly with capacity.
- GPU SKU: per-GPU / per-vGPU SKU for leased GPU scenarios (useful for customers who want fine-grained chargeback).

2) Platform fee amortization example
- We offer 3 amortization templates in the workbook: 12, 24, 36 months. Example: $300k platform fee amortized over 36 months = $8.3k/mo for budgeting; or we can annualize to $100k/yr for 3 years. Workbook shows EBITDA-friendly and CapEx-friendly views.

3) Support tiers (high level)
- Standard: business hours email + 24h ticket SLA, monthly patch bundle, access to docs and community channels.
- Premium: 24/7 on-call (P2/P1 triage window 4h), quarterly architecture reviews, 8h hotfix SLA for critical regressions, limited included engineering triage (10 hrs/mo).
- Enterprise: dedicated SRE retainer, guaranteed response & escalation path, private runbooks, on-prem binary escrow options, and prioritized feature work.

4) Pilot credits & one-time support
- We can offer a one-time pilot implementation credit up to 20% of the initial platform fee for a proof-of-concept (subject to signature). For multi-site pilots we'll consider additional engineering hours.

5) Security/compliance
- SOC2 Type II report and an integration guide for KMS (customer-managed) + SAML SSO will be attached in an evidence pack (separate secure link).

NEXT STEPS:
- I attached VPC_pricing_breakdown_v3.xlsx and a SOW-starter-pilot-2027-05.pdf. Can you please confirm which license construct Vitality prefers (site | node | GPU) and whether you want the platform fee amortized over 12/24/36 months? Once you confirm, I can prepare a commercial term sheet + DocuSign SOW.

Best,
Tessa Morgan

Subject: internal: Vitality Health — recommended commercial posture (private note)

Marissa / Irene — quick internal note before I hear back from procurement. Anna asked for decomposition and timeline targeting 2027-05-31. Key constraints: they want CapEx clarity and a sample escrow clause. My recommended posture:

- Offer site license as primary construct (keeps their CapEx simple).
- Pilot credit: up to 20% off platform fee; concession authority: Marissa sign-off up to 15%, Irene up to 25% with legal review.
- Platform fee amortization: allow customer to pick 12/24/36; provide pricing anchor for 36-mo as default for finance friendliness.
- Support: default to Premium with option to upgrade to Enterprise (we include 10 hrs/mo SRE for first 3 months as part of pilot if we give 20% credit).

Notes / asks to you: Marissa — can you confirm margin impact of 20% pilot credit on a $300k platform fee (I did a quick calc — roughly 6% net margin hit after amortized ops). Irene — legal to prep a short escrow addendum (we typically allow binary escrow + release on breach or insolvency). Ben — loop in product if any hard blockers on 10 hrs/mo SRE during pilot.

If we get approval, I will send a redline-friendly SOW and a commercial term sheet with the DocuSign prep link.

Thanks — Tessa

Tessa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the workbook, that helped. A couple follow-ups from our side before we escalate to exec approval:

- License construct: leaning toward site license for their simplicity, but need a per-site minimum (what's the min GPU baseline you require?)
- Platform fee amortization: our finance prefers 12 or 24 months. A 36-month amortization is harder to justify to our auditors; can you provide an example P&L impact for 12 and 24 months?
- Pilot credit: procurement counter-offer is 15% of platform fee and a request to cap included SRE hours at 5 hrs/mo for the pilot (we can extend paid hours thereafter).
- Escrow: procurement needs the escrow clause to explicitly list release triggers (bankruptcy, sustained data breach) and a 30-day cure window. Do you accept that language?

Also request: two customer references for similar air-gapped on-prem installs (company names only are fine), and confirmation that SOC2 Type II report can be shared under NDA.

Timeline: procurement still expects to sign by 2027-05-31 but may need the PO by 2027-06-03. If we can get a term sheet with the 15% pilot credit and 12/24 amortization examples by EOD Monday (2027-05-24), we'll be able to slot this into our approval cycle.

Thanks,
Michael Cheng
Director of Infrastructure
Vitality Health
